newsitem.title: USA: COMEX COPPER ENDS WEAKER BUT STAYS RANGE-BOUND.
newsitem.headline: COMEX COPPER ENDS WEAKER BUT STAYS RANGE-BOUND.

text.p: COMEX copper ended lower on commission house and fund selling, but failed to break through support at 105.00 cents a lb in the September contract.
Commission house brokers describe a market that is sold heavily at the top of the range, currently at 108.00 cents and bought at 105.00-105.50 cents.
The active September contract settled at 106.10 cents a lb, down 2.00 cents from Thursday, while the spot month ended at 105.90 cent a lb, down 2.05 cents.

"It's going to have to break one way or the other soon," one broker said. "Today we saw some of the commission houses and funds taking some profits. But we get a lot of chunky buying on the dips and some chunky selling at the top. But nothing breaks."
The trade has been completely on the sidelines, she said.

Fundamentally, the market remains dull. The American Bureau of Metal Statistics noted that U.S. copper rod production for the first half of the year is up 4.4 percent from last year. And U.S. brass mill shipments were up 7.6 percent in the same time frame.
But while demand may be strong in the U.S., supplies remain ample. "There's plenty of metal around," said one physical dealer.
London Metal Exchange warehouse stocks increased another 2,925 tonnes to 248,700 tonnes, the highest level since September 23. The cash-to-three-month backwardation is steady at $25/$30.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646)
